description: Public, presentation-neutral SchoolBrief roadmap data for optional use by schoolbrief.io and other public surfaces.

items.title: Add second county school district POC
items.summary: Select and onboard a second county-scale public school district as SchoolBrief's next proof of concept. No specific district or public release date is committed yet.
items.description: Add a second county school district POC to test SchoolBrief beyond its original Greenville County implementation and the smaller Ware Shoals onboarding exercise.
items.why: SchoolBrief needs to prove that its district model scales beyond one large county system and one small district without depending on Greenville-specific assumptions.
items.origin_detail: After Greenville County and the Ware Shoals proof-of-concept onboarding, SchoolBrief identified a second county-scale district as the next useful expansion test. The specific district is intentionally left open until selection.

items.title: Public roadmap, known issues, and Get SchoolBrief page
items.summary: SchoolBrief now provides a native roadmap, known-issues, and district-request experience on schoolbrief.io.
items.description: A SchoolBrief-owned public page lets families see selected roadmap items and known issues, understand why they matter, and request SchoolBrief support for a new district or area.
items.why: Most families should not need to understand GitHub repositories or issue trackers to see what SchoolBrief is improving, and expansion requests should be clearly separated from missing-source submissions for already-supported schools.
items.origin_detail: SchoolBrief adopted a private engineering tracker plus a curated public roadmap and decided the public information should eventually be available directly on schoolbrief.io.

items.title: Consistent SchoolBrief visual design across app and web
items.summary: Align SchoolBrief-owned app and web surfaces around one accessible, modular visual system.
items.description: Bring the SchoolBrief website, public calendar, school-selection UI, submission/support pages, and other owned surfaces into one consistent visual language built from reusable design tokens and components.
items.why: Families should feel like they are using one product, some current school-selection states need better contrast and readability, and future homepage/theme experiments should inherit the same visual system instead of creating parallel styling.
items.origin_detail: Visual review of the iOS school/calendar experience and SchoolBrief web surfaces identified inconsistent brand treatment and hard-to-read selection colors. Later homepage planning added a requirement that the shared system remain modular enough for dynamic real-event content and possible light/dark appearance modes.

items.title: SchoolBrief 1.0 public App Store launch
items.summary: Complete and directly verify SchoolBrief's first public App Store release.
items.description: Complete the first public App Store release of SchoolBrief and verify that families can install and use the released application through the normal App Store path.
items.why: A source-complete build or successful archive is not the same thing as a publicly available product, so SchoolBrief should only describe 1.0 as released after the actual public distribution path is complete and observed.
items.origin_detail: SchoolBrief reached its first public iOS release-candidate stage after the Greenville-focused product, backend, privacy, and release-readiness work converged.

items.title: Preserve useful calendar context when official sources change
items.summary: Preserve useful historical calendar context without presenting old information as current scheduled events.
items.description: Improve how previously observed calendar information is retained and explained when an official source changes, removes events, or becomes sparse.
items.why: Parents may still need to understand what had previously been scheduled, moved, or removed, while stale events must not be mistaken for current plans.
items.origin_detail: District onboarding and source-change testing highlighted the need for clearer lifecycle handling when previously published school events disappear from an official source.

items.title: Family profiles for multiple children and schools
items.summary: Explore local-first family profiles for multiple children and eventually multiple schools.
items.description: Support families with multiple children, first without duplicating shared school information and eventually across more than one school, while preserving SchoolBrief's local-first privacy model.
items.why: Many families have children in different grades or at different schools and should be able to personalize relevance without requiring a family account or multiplying shared events.
items.origin_detail: Family-profile planning identified multiple-child support as a natural post-1.0 extension of the current single-school/grade experience.

items.title: Future Android client
items.summary: Keep a path open for a future Android SchoolBrief client after the iPhone experience matures.
items.description: Explore and eventually build an Android SchoolBrief client that uses the same shared public-data contract while preserving local-first family personalization.
items.why: Families should not be permanently excluded from SchoolBrief because they use a different mobile platform.
items.origin_detail: SchoolBrief's architecture was designed as iOS-first rather than iOS-only, with a shared API contract and local personalization model.

items.title: Stable, rights-safe meal images
items.summary: Add meal images only where they can be delivered reliably and with appropriate reuse and attribution rights.
items.description: Add meal-item images only where SchoolBrief can use durable image references from a documented or permitted source without relying on short-lived links.
items.why: Images could make menus easier to scan, but temporary links or unclear usage rights would create a brittle or inappropriate feature.
items.origin_detail: Menu-source investigation found that some available image URLs are temporary or otherwise unsuitable for durable public publication.

items.title: Distinguish a working empty calendar from an unavailable calendar
items.summary: Represent a valid calendar with no current events differently from a calendar that failed to load or validate.
items.description: Make a clear distinction between a working calendar that currently contains no events and a calendar that could not be loaded or validated.
items.why: A small school or district may legitimately publish no current events, and families should not see that as a source failure while SchoolBrief still protects against genuinely broken or unexpectedly emptied calendars.
items.origin_detail: Expansion beyond Greenville encountered a valid school calendar with zero current events, demonstrating that empty-but-healthy needs to be represented separately from unavailable.

items.title: Expand About, Privacy, and How It Works
items.summary: SchoolBrief now provides deeper public explanations of why it exists, how it works, and how privacy is preserved.
items.description: The public About and Privacy pages are expanded and a readable How It Works page explains the product and architecture for people who want more than marketing copy.
items.why: Users should be able to understand where information comes from, how uncertainty is handled, what stays on the device, and why the product is designed the way it is.
items.origin_detail: SchoolBrief's purpose-and-intent, privacy, and architecture discussions identified a need for technically meaningful but publicly understandable documentation rather than publishing the private backend source.
